groups.title: Triangles
groups.explanation: Each word describes a triangle by its sides or its angles.

groups.title: Four-sided shapes
groups.explanation: All four are quadrilaterals, closed shapes with four straight sides.

groups.title: Solid shapes
groups.explanation: Each of these takes up space rather than sitting flat on the page.

sources.excerpt: In man-made construction, the isosceles triangles may be found in the shape of gables and pediments, and the equilateral triangle can be found in the yield sign.
In a scalene triangle, the trigonometric functions can be used to find the unknown measure of either a side or an internal angle; methods for doing so use the law of sines and the law of cosines.
A triangle in which all of its angles are less than 90° is an acute triangle.
A rhombus with right angles is a square.
A rhombus is a special case of a parallelogram and a kite.
In geometry, a trapezoid () in North American English, or trapezium () in British English, is a quadrilateral that has at least one pair of parallel sides.
A solid figure is the region of 3D space bounded by a two-dimensional closed surface; for example, a solid ball consists of a sphere and its interior.

Solid geometry deals with the measurements of volumes of various solids, including pyramids, prisms, cubes (and other polyhedrons), cylinders, cones (including truncated) and other solids of revolution.

editorNotes: No tile fits two groups here: a square is a face of a cube but is itself flat, and a kite is a bird and a toy as well as a quadrilateral, though no group asks for either. Acute describes an angle as well as a triangle, and prism belongs with the solids rather than with light.
